spans.text: On the moving vehicle...
The Commander has covered Elsa's body with a white cloth.
Though their distress is nowhere near Machlian's, the knowledge that an innocent child has suffered such a terrible fate fills their heart with raging fury.
...I'm sorry, Robin.
But I have to bury Elsa myself. If you will only allow me one thing...let me do that.
That's fine.
Machlian looks silently at the covered corpse and clenches her fists.
After a simple bandage, her palm is no longer bleeding.
You don't need to take part in the upcoming mission.
The situation in the prison may be more complicated than what we've encountered so far.
I've already paid the price for running from my problems, Robin.
Machlian shakes her head lightly.
...It's far too heavy.
In Bohnsdorf, I could almost live a real human being.
But in the end, reality showed me that it was all a lie.
I don't even know if what I've done has meaning anymore.
Elia might have deceived you, but what you did was far from meaningless.
...Elsa was innocent. Even to the very end, she believed in you, her Saint.
Yes, she believed in me.
And what good did that do her?
Machlian looks up, a sad smile on her face.
I couldn't do anything...
The Commander falls silent and shakes their head.
They have seen hell so many times, they are hardly fazed by the tragedy that befell Bohnsdorf.
But for Machlian, this blow is too much to bear.
...Does this mean they've become indifferent to it all?
As Machlian gazes at the Commander, her expression suddenly shifts.
You're also a semi-immunosome, Robin.
A what?
You're like me. You're partially immune.
That's why you weren't affected by exposure to Collapse Particles at such close range back in the village.
...It's a long story.
...You really aren't with Paradeus, Robin.
Machlian smiles. The Commander doesn't know what to say to that.
Just then, Perosa walks over and breaks up the awkwardness.
Our next destination is the prison.
While I don't think what happened at the quarantine wall is likely to repeat itself... We should still be careful.
Shall we contact the Earl?
Yeah. I was just about to bring him up to speed.
Understood.
The transmission goes through.
Commander.
Considering the timing of this call...
I assume you have good news for me.
...Good and bad in equal measure.
The truth is, Mr. Griffin, we've already investigated three of the locations you sent us.
We encountered Paradeus forces at each of them, as well as the explosives they had hidden there.
Machlian's memories are reliable.
The Commander looks at Machlian and hesitates.
While we did succeed in stopping them for the most part, a tragedy still took place in Bohnsdorf.
I've handed the scene over to the government authorities, but the casualties are still severe...
Since the veracity of Machlian's memory fragments has been verified...
You should turn her over to me.
We might be able to find some information on William now.
Machlian blanches and frantically shakes her head at the Commander.
I'm sorry, Mr. Griffin... But I might not be able to do that for the time being.
Our mission is at a critical phase and we still need Machlian's assistance.
Once we take care of Paradeus, we can further analyze Machlian's memory fragments.
...I see no problem with your decision.
Do you have anything else to report?
We'll be heading over to Berlin Prison to conduct an investigation. We were hoping that you would give us clearance to do so, Mr. Griffin.
I see. Let Perosa handle it.
...Keep up the good work, Commander. I have a very good feeling about you.
Thank you.
Oh yes, there is one more thing I need to tell you.
What is it?
Angelia's actions have been too impulsive as of late.
There are some things which she will not listen to if they come from me, so I need you to help make her see sense.
I value both of you a great deal, and I hope you can help each other more.
Understood. Thank you.
The transmission ends.
...Thank you, Robin.
No problem.
The Commander shakes their head and looks at the map... They're almost at Berlin Prison.
I hope things work out this time round...
Berlin Prison.
In the main control room.
I find it very difficult to comply with your request.
You're asking me to let in such a large group of Dolls to search the prison all of a sudden?
This is outrageous.
I am being absolutely serious. There is a high chance that the prison is rigged with explosives planted by terrorists.
If you don't believe me, your men are welcome to come along and follow our inspection.
You can't possibly expect me to believe that sort of nonsense.
We're here with the appropriate clearances, so it doesn't matter whether you believe it or not.
Even if we did turn out to be illegal intruders, you wouldn't be blamed for letting us in.
But conversely, if the prison has really been compromised and we miss the critical time frame because of your interference... Will you take responsibility for THAT?
The chief warden hesitates. Though he doesn't want to do this, the permit presented by the Commander is valid and effective.
...Alright, I understand.
But I'm telling you, you're just wasting your time!
Thank you for your cooperation.
The Commander breathes a sigh of relief. For a moment, they thought there would be no way to settle this peacefully.
Unlike the previous sites, they're in the middle of the city now... Surely Paradeus isn't so bold that they'd strike here, right?
Mr. Warden, just out of curiosity...
Has anything strange happened in the prison recently?
Anything strange?
The warden rubs his chin thoughtfully.
Nothing comes to mind. Apart from the arrival of the most recent batch of convicts, it has been pretty uneventful here at the prison.
As you know, very few criminals actually make it into prison alive these days.
Dandelion, is something bothering you?
I just hacked into the prison systems.
The automatic security systems are all offline.
They have all been very thoroughly sabotaged and cannot be repaired.
Say what?! You hacked into what?!
Wait a minute, the security's offline? Nobody told me about that!
...Crap.
Knock knock knock!
Warden, Warden! This is bad!
What happened?!
The prisoners... The prisoners are rioting!
The Warden gapes, then he collapses to the ground, fainting on the spot.
Tsk.
It's just one thing after another!
Commander, you and Machlian should stay here. The situation is going to be very chaotic and we must prioritize your safety.
The convicts couldn't have done this by themselves. Paradeus must have sneaked some of their people in here.
45, you and Dandelion head to the control room and verify the situation.
Also, root out any Paradeus units hiding among the convicts.
Understood.
Perosa, back up the prison officers! Suppress the riots and—
Boom!
They've got bombs!
—And disarm those bombs.
You must not allow the convicts to get on the streets!
Roger!
